newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S'hai Hai Xing hit by high finance cost.
newsitem.headline: S'hai Hai Xing hit by high finance cost.

text.p: China's Shanghai Hai Xing Shipping Co Ltd, the first H-share to post a net loss, said on Wednesday its earnings were hit by higher finance costs and sluggish domestic demand for shipping services.

"The sluggish demand for domestic shipping led to a situation where supply exceeded demand. As a result, the company's newly commissioned vessels could not be fully utilised," said company chairman Li Shaode in a statement published in Hong Kong.
H-shares are shares of companies incorporated in China and listed in Hong Kong. There are currently 21 H-shares traded in the British colony.
Owing to the significant increase in the number of new vessels, depreciation for the first half amounted to 298 million yuan, up 20 percent from the same period in 1995, it said.
Li said three upward interest rate adjustments on existing loans in 1995 resulted in higher finance costs.
The company said total finance costs reached 271 million yuan, up 75 percent over the same period in 1995.
The shipping company reported an interim loss of 84.49 million yuan for the first half of 1996, compared with 50.51 million yuan profit a year ago.
Looking ahead, the company said it would continue to face difficulties due to the oversupply of capacity.
"The high interest rate on long term loans will continue to burden the company," Li said.
Shanghai Hai Xing, however, was confident it would benefit from China's aims of establishing direct shipping links with Taiwan.
"The company believes that it should benefit from these new measures," Li said. "The company has been actively improving itself to undertake shipping transportation in the Taiwan Strait."
Last week, the Ministry of Communications announced direct shipping links with Taiwan would be permitted.
